chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Hishām ibn Sālim, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who reviles ʿAlī عليه السلام? He said to me: “His blood is lawful, by Allah, were it not that he might thereby implicate an innocent person.” He said: I said: Then what do you say about a man who harms us? He said: “In what way is that?” He said: So I said: Concerning you, he mentions you. He said: “He has a share in ʿAlī عليه السلام.” I said to him: Indeed, he says that and makes it public. He said: “Do not expose yourself to him.”

May I be made your ransom, what do you say about a man who falsely accuses some people from the pre-Islamic Arabs? He said: “The prescribed punishment is administered, for that reaches the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.حَلَالُ الدَّمِ: liable to being killed under the ruling stated in the report
key_terms.سَبَّابَةٍ: one who habitually reviles or insults
key_terms.مُؤْذٍ: one who causes harm or offense
key_terms.نَصِيبٌ: a share or portion, meaning participation in the offense against ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: to accuse falsely or cast a defamatory allegation

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about reviling Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام and slandering the Arabs of Jāhiliyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith records legal responses concerning reviling Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, harming the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, and slandering people of the Arabs from the Jāhiliyyah period. It indicates the gravity of abuse connected to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام and affirms the application of the hadd punishment for false accusation, because such offense ultimately reaches the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
